historical_choice.head: c44a3d7254f9103e6053d449b911a5aa019f957e
historical_choice.normal_source_disposition: An accepted ordinary restore/reset creates a new state object; render synchronizes before geometry checks and clears the prior comparison. A preview or cancellation leaves the active state token unchanged.

finding.classification: Confirmed defect in the isolated PR19 + accepted watch-file composition, not a claim of failure in either standalone qualified tree.
finding.trigger: Have a visible day-1 historical comparison, adopt a valid native day-3 file, then inject the already documented one-shot SavedWatch.replayHistory refusal in the post-adoption display callback.
finding.mechanism: The R2 callback catch sets state=null and disables game controls without rendering. Incoming WatchChoice synchronizes only from render and synchronize(null) returns immediately. Its private history and visible result therefore remain from the old watch.
finding.observed: The active imported day-3 watch is saved and actually exported byte-for-byte; the old day-1 comparison remains visible and identical while all game controls are disabled.
finding.consequence: The historical panel presents a predecessor watch's output after replacement and has not followed the advertised accepted-state invalidation boundary.
finding.minimal_coordinated_remedy: Add an explicit WatchChoice invalidation/null-token path that clears private history and result and hides/disables its panel without native replay allocation. Invoke it from the accepted-adoption display-failure catch. Existing synchronize(null) alone is insufficient.
finding.required_owner_boundary: #17 retains WatchChoice implementation; #12 retains file admission/restore. Root should coordinate the minimal composition interface with that owner. No remedy is implemented by this receiver.
